questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) MODIFIED LANGUAGE READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The diagram shows the change in an economy’s production possibility curve as it grows in the long run. Which movement from point X is most likely to show the highest potential for growth? A B C consumer X goods D O capital goods

The diagrams show the change in a country’s production possibility curve between Year 1 and Year 2. Year 1 Year 2 consumer consumer goods goods 0 50 0 80 services services What can be concluded from the diagrams?

options.A: Future growth prospects have been harmed.
options.B: The level of unemployment has fallen.
options.C: The opportunity cost of consumer goods has risen.
options.D: The proportionate growth in production is greater in consumer goods.

questions.questionText: What term is used by economists for the income received by the factor of production enterprise?

options.A: capital
options.B: interest
options.C: profit
options.D: revenue

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve for housing. price D O quantity What is not assumed to remain constant when drawing this curve?

options.A: consumer incomes
options.B: expectations about future house prices
options.C: the price of houses
options.D: the rate of interest charged on loans for house purchase

questions.questionText: What does not cause the demand curve for cars to shift to the right?

options.A: a fall in the price of petrol (gas)
options.B: a fall in the price of public transport
options.C: an advertising campaign by car manufacturers
options.D: an economy-wide increase in incomes

questions.questionText: An individual reacts to a 5% increase in the price of good X by increasing the proportion of his income that he spends on good X from 2% to 3%. If there are no other changes, what can be concluded from this about the individual’s demand for good X?

options.A: It is income-elastic.
options.B: It is income-inelastic.
options.C: It is price-elastic.
options.D: It is price-inelastic.

questions.questionText: The cross-elasticity of demand for good X with respect to good Y is –0.5. What can be concluded from this?

options.A: Goods X and Y are complementary goods.
options.B: Goods X and Y are substitute goods.
options.C: Good X is an inferior good.
options.D: Good Y is an inferior good.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a supply curve for beef. S price O quantity What explains why the supply curve for beef slopes upwards?

options.A: An increase in the demand for beef will bring about an increase in supply.
options.B: Farmers’ productivity rises as the price rises.
options.C: Increased production leads to a reduction in costs.
options.D: The cost of additional beef production rises as output increases.

questions.questionText: Which business is likely to be the slowest to alter its output in response to a sustained increase in demand for its product?

options.A: a fast-food restaurant
options.B: a household cleaning service
options.C: a newspaper printer
options.D: an oil exploration company

questions.questionText: In a particular year, 12000 units of a good are sold at $1 per unit. In a later year, 14000 units are sold at $1.20 per unit. If consumer tastes have remained constant, what could account for the change between the two years?

options.A: a decrease in the price of raw materials used by producers
options.B: an increase in the price of a substitute good
options.C: an increase in the rate of tax imposed on producers
options.D: the formation of a monopoly in the production of the good

questions.questionText: The diagram shows demand and supply curves for petrol (gas). The initial equilibrium is at X. What could be the new equilibrium if there were a large fall in the price of cars? S A S S

options.B: 1 price X D C D D D O quantity

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an individual’s demand curve for a commodity. x price P z y D O Q quantity The supplier of the commodity charges a unit price of OP but consumers are currently required to purchase a minimum quantity, OQ. Which area(s) in the diagram measure the net gain in consumer surplus from the removal of the minimum purchase requirement?

options.A: x + y B x – z C y only D z only

questions.questionText: In 2011, the Health Ministry in a country encouraged parents to have their children vaccinated against measles. The parents did not have to use the vaccine and did not have to pay for it. The government cancelled other projects to fund the programme from taxation because research concluded that the vaccine benefited the community by preventing the spread of a serious illness. Which concepts are implied in the above statement?

options.A: external benefit, public sector, opportunity cost
options.B: market mechanism, fiscal policy, public good
options.C: merit good, normative statement, regulatory control
options.D: private cost, social benefit, monetary policy

questions.questionText: A gardener plants bamboo to create an attractive environment along the roadside. The bamboo grows into the garden of his neighbour, who removes the bamboo with a chemical spray. What cannot be concluded about the outcome of the planting?

options.A: It increases external cost and external benefit.
options.B: It increases private cost and private benefit.
options.C: It increases social cost and social benefit.
options.D: It increases social cost more than social benefit.

questions.questionText: A cost-benefit analysis of a proposed underground railway produced the following statistics. annual costs and benefits $ million annual capital cost 10 operating and maintenance costs 3 fare revenue 6 savings to private travellers 5 savings to business 10 other economic benefits 7 What can be concluded from the statistics?

options.A: If undertaken by the private sector there would be a loss of $13 million.
options.B: If undertaken by the private sector there would be a profit of $3 million.
options.C: If undertaken by the public sector there would be a net social benefit of $15 million.
options.D: If undertaken by the public sector there would be a net social cost of $1 million.

questions.questionText: What is the best example of what was once a public good becoming a private good?

options.A: education
options.B: medical care
options.C: postal services
options.D: television broadcasts

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for onions in equilibrium at point X. The government has a stock of onions and wants to establish a new equilibrium at point Y. supply Z X price Y demand O quantity Which actions should the government take?

options.A: It should buy an amount equal to XY and subsidise producers by a sum equal to YZ.
options.B: It should buy an amount equal to XY and tax producers by a sum equal to YZ.
options.C: It should sell an amount equal to XY and subsidise producers by a sum equal to YZ.
options.D: It should sell an amount equal to XY and tax producers by a sum equal to YZ.

questions.questionText: The diagram illustrates the production possibility curves for countries S and T producing goods X and Y. country S country T 400 400 300 300 good X 200 good X 200 100 100 0 0 0 50 100 150 200 0 50 100 150 200 good Y good Y Countries S and T specialise in the product for which they have the lower opportunity cost. They trade with each other at the rate of two good X for one good Y. What is a possible combination of goods for country S to consume after specialisation and trade have taken place? good X good Y
What is the most likely reason why Pakistan might reduce its trade barriers on imports?

options.A: to help Pakistan increase its gain from comparative advantage
options.B: to help Pakistan invest more abroad
options.C: to raise its foreign exchange rate
options.D: to reduce government borrowing and international debt

questions.questionText: A particular good in the Barbados market could be supplied by domestic producers, or producers in Trinidad & Tobago, or producers in the USA, at the prices shown in US dollars. origin of production price Barbados $1.00 Trinidad & Tobago $0.85 USA $0.75 Originally, Barbados had a 20% ad valorem duty on imports from Trinidad & Tobago and the USA. Barbados then formed a customs union with Trinidad & Tobago, with a common external tariff, also of 20%. From which countries would Barbados import the good, before the formation of the customs union and after the formation of the customs union? before after

options.A: neither Trinidad & Tobago
options.B: neither USA
options.C: USA Trinidad & Tobago
options.D: USA USA

questions.questionText: A Japanese car manufacturer established a successful factory in France. How would this be shown in the Japanese balance of payments? investment in the factory dividends and profits from the factory

options.A: negative entry in the financial account positive entry in the current account
options.B: negative entry in the current account positive entry in the financial account
options.C: positive entry in the financial account negative entry in the current account
options.D: positive entry in the current account negative entry in the financial account

questions.questionText: The graph shows changes in the unemployment rates in countries X, Y and Z over the period 2000 to 2010. All three countries faced recession between 2008 and 2010.
Which supply-side measure is most likely to produce short-run growth in a country’s aggregate supply?

options.A: easing of controls on immigration of workers
options.B: expenditure on primary education
options.C: expenditure on research and development
options.D: privatisation of public utilities

questions.questionText: An economy is experiencing accelerating cost-push inflation. Which group is likely to be least concerned by this?

options.A: borrowers
options.B: consumers
options.C: creditors
options.D: exporters

questions.questionText: The table shows the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for a country. year CPI 2008 100 2009 104 2010 102 2011 105 2012 108 2013 111 Which statement about the period 2008 to 2013 is correct?

options.A: Prices increased each year.
options.B: Prices increased fastest in 2011.
options.C: The rate of inflation was 2% in 2010.
options.D: The smallest rise in prices was in 2013.

questions.questionText: At a time when international demand for oil was high, Bolivia encouraged investment by foreign firms in order to exploit its oil and gas resources. What overall impact would this have on the balance of payments of Bolivia?

options.A: definitely favourable, as Bolivia could increase its exports of gas and oil
options.B: definitely unfavourable, as the foreign companies would transfer profits out of the country
options.C: uncertain, as there would be inflows and outflows of currency
options.D: zero, as Bolivia itself would use the gas and oil produced

questions.questionText: An economy with a fixed exchange rate experiences an increased deficit on the current account of the balance of payments. What is most likely to increase as a consequence?

options.A: employment
options.B: interest rates
options.C: investment
options.D: national output

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the number of US dollars ($) and Euros (€) which exchanged for one pound sterling (£) between 2002 and 2004. 1.8 $ per £ 1.7 1.6 1.5 1.4 € per £ 1.3 2002 2003 2004 What happened to the exchange rate of the $ against the £ and € during this period? $ exchange rate $ exchange rate against £ against €

options.A: appreciated appreciated
options.B: appreciated depreciated
options.C: depreciated appreciated
options.D: depreciated depreciated

questions.questionText: In a time of recession, a government decided to sell a loss-making state-owned industry to a foreign private company. What is the most likely immediate result?

options.A: an improvement in the financial account of the balance of payments
options.B: an improvement in the level of unemployment
options.C: an improvement in the rate of inflation
options.D: an improvement in the trade account of the balance of payments reasonable effort has been made by the publisher (UCLES) to trace copyright holders, but if any items requiring clearance have unwittingly been included, the publisher will be pleased to make amends at the earliest possible opportunity.
